summary: Verified the auto-admin-on-login fix for kijitechnology@gmail.com: with a fresh session on the real, already-backfilled admin user, GET /api/auth/me immediately returns has_access=true/access_mode='admin' with NO admin-unlock call, GET /api/topics returns 200, and the app's paywall gate (RequirePaid) lets the admin straight into '/' instead of redirecting to /membership. A different (non-admin) email does NOT get this treatment: has_access=false, access_mode=null, /api/topics 403, and the paywall gate redirects it to /membership. The admin-unlock password fallback for the same admin email still works (200/admin on correct password, 403 on wrong password) -- confirmed via updated existing test file.

GET /api/auth/me -> HTTP 200, user.has_access=true, user.access_mode='admin' (no /admin-unlock call made). GET /api/topics with same cookie -> HTTP 200.

action_items.detail: Full suite (cd /app/backend && python -m pytest -q) has 18 pre-existing failures in tests/test_tscheck_paid_access_control.py and tests/test_tscheck_content_coverage.py -- same stale-fixture-cookie issue flagged in iteration_1/2/3, unrelated to this iteration's acceptance_matrix (auto-admin-on-login). Not touched, flagged for main agent awareness only.

The existing admin_cookie fixture in tests/test_tscheck_admin_unlock.py previously tried to upsert a NEW user document for kijitechnology@gmail.com (a new user_id with that email), which now fails with a MongoDB duplicate-key error on the unique email index because the real admin user already exists (per seed_facts backfill). Updated the fixture to attach a fresh session to the existing real user instead of creating a duplicate user doc, and to clean up only the session afterward. This is a testing-artifact fix (no application code touched) needed for the suite to keep passing after the backfill described in the briefing.

notes: All 3 acceptance_matrix criteria covered (8 checks: 2 new backend tests for the auto-admin-on-login behavior + 2 UI-level browser checks proving the paywall gate respects it end-to-end, plus 3 existing admin-unlock regression tests re-verified and 1 existing test's fixture repaired for compatibility with the now-real admin user). Confirmed via direct code read of routers/auth.py exchange() that profile['is_admin']=True is set before the upsert whenever email==ADMIN_EMAIL, so future re-logins by this email will also auto-admin (per spec_deviations, real Google OAuth session_id cannot be obtained in this sandbox, so the exchange() endpoint itself was verified by code inspection + by exercising its downstream effect via a session pointed at the real already-migrated user). Real production user doc (kijitechnology@gmail.com) was never modified or deleted -- only temporary session docs were created and removed; verified with a final DB read after cleanup.
